chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, from his father, from Rifa'ah ibn Musa, from Abdullah ibn Atta', who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him), saying: 'When the Qa'im (the Rising One) rises, with what conduct will he proceed among the people?' He said: 'He will annul what was before him, as the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did, and he will resume Islam anew.'
ai.seo_question: What conduct will the Qa'im follow when he rises according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Nu'mani's *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Baqir clarifies that the Qa'im will not merely reform but fundamentally dismantle the pre-existing socio-political structures ('هدم ما قبله') to establish a pristine Islamic order, mirroring the Prophet's initial mission. This underscores the Shia eschatological view that the Mahdi's rule represents a complete restoration of divine justice and original revelation, distinct from the accumulated traditions of previous eras. The emphasis on 'renewing Islam anew' highlights the continuity of prophetic authority while signaling a fresh start for the global community.
